name: Javan Woodcock
rangeDescription: Mountains of sumatra and western java
description: Rare and reclusive long-billed inhabitant of moist montane and foothill forests at 1350-3000 meters. Dark brown and heavily patterned overall, with densest patterning on the back.

name: Pectoral Sandpiper
rangeDescription: Breeds arctic north america and siberia; winters to southern south america, australia
description: Beefy, medium-sized sandpiper. Brown-toned overall with yellowish legs.

name: Long-tailed Duck
rangeDescription: Coasts of holarctic region
description: Diving duck that favors saltwater in winter and Arctic tundra pools in summer. Males are distinctive with black, white, gray, and brown patterns and long pointed tail.

name: Cinnamon-breasted Tody-Tyrant
rangeDescription: Southern ecuador (cordillera del cóndor) to northern peru (san martín)
description: A small flycatcher found only on several outlying ridges along the eastern Andes in northern Peru and southern Ecuador. It has a cinnamon breast and throat, a yellowish belly, and buffy “spectacles” that can be inconspicuous on some individuals.

name: Sooretama Slaty-Antshrike
rangeDescription: Coastal southeastern brazil (southern bahia and espírito santo to rio de janeiro)
description: Small antshrike found in the lower and middle level of woodlands and second growth. Males are gray with a dark cap and black wings and tail that have prominent white bars and spots.

name: Southern Ground-Hornbill
rangeDescription: Savanna of eastern and southern africa
description: This enormous, sociable, ground-loving hornbill is easily recognized. The adult male has an extensive brilliant red face and throat wattles, while the adult female has purple-blue skin in the center of the red throat patch.

name: Loango Weaver
rangeDescription: Coastal southern gabon to mouth of congo river
description: A wetland weaver with a narrow bill, dull olive upperparts, and yellow-orange underparts. Male has a dark hood that tapers to a “V” on the throat, surrounded by an orange wash, while female lacks the black hood and has a yellow forehead and olive crown.

name: Forest Owlet
rangeDescription: Known from 7 19th century specimens from northwestern maharashtra, orissa, and chhattisgarh; rediscovered in taloda area, maharashtra after hiatus of 113 years; now known from deciduous forest mainly in surat dangs (gujarat), northwestern maharashtra, and melghat tiger reserve (western madhya pradesh)
description: Extremely localized small owl, restricted to parts of west-central India. Known locations are in lowland forest between 200 and 600 meters of elevation; appears to favor teak forests.

name: Taczanowski's Tinamou
rangeDescription: Andes of south-central peru (junín to puno)
description: Rarely-seen terrestrial bird found in the high Andes of southern Peru and adjacent border regions of Bolivia. No other tinamou has such a long, curved bill; also note the stout yellow legs and profuse white markings on back and breast.

name: Rusty-breasted Wren-Babbler
rangeDescription: Montane forest of western sumatra
description: Chunky babbler of the forest floor and understory in Sumatra’s highlands. Mostly dark brown, with a white throat, dark scaling on the upperparts, and the namesake rust-colored breast.

name: Isabela Oriole
rangeDescription: Northern philippines (mountains of northern luzon)
description: A medium-sized bird of lowland forest, including secondary habitats and bamboo in northern Luzon. Yellow underparts blend into olive upperparts.

name: Great Myna
rangeDescription: Northeastern india to southwestern china, myanmar, thailand, and indochina
description: A black myna with a spiffy crest. Not actually significantly larger than other dark crested mynas, but the combination of the bright yellow bill, prominent spiky crest, and white vent serve to distinguish it from other similar mynas.

name: Cinereous Harrier
rangeDescription: Andes of colombia to tierra del fuego and falkland islands
description: Fairly common in open country of Patagonia, often near lakes and marshes; uncommon and local northward. Male silvery gray overall with fine rusty barring below.

name: Plain Leaf Warbler
rangeDescription: Oak-juniper woodland of iran to afghanistan and kashmir
description: A small, unmarked warbler with dark bill and legs. Sandy gray above and pale gray below.

name: Blue-winged Laughingthrush
rangeDescription: Montane forest of nepal to southwestern china, myanmar, and northwestern tonkin
description: Brown laughingthrush with a black brow and a bright silvery-azure panel on the wing. Wings, belly, and rump are more rufous-tinged than the rest of the body.

name: Eastern Paradise-Whydah
rangeDescription: Southeastern sudan, ethiopia, and somalia southward to northeastern south africa, also westward across southern africa to angola and northern namibia
description: The breeding male is buff, chestnut, and black with a 21-centimeter tail that is laterally flattened with both short bulging feathers and long, tapering dagger-like feathers. The female and non-breeding male have a strongly contrasting black-and-white head, including a characteristic dark bill and a double “C” pattern under the ear.

name: Little Bunting
rangeDescription: Taiga of northern eurasia; winters to india, southeastern asia, and philippines
description: Small bunting with an attractive contrasting head pattern: black crown with red-brown central stripe and pale eyering. Rufous cheeks bordered by narrow black lines framing the eyes.

name: White-eyed Starling
rangeDescription: Bougainville, guadalcanal, choiseul, and rendova (northern solomon islands)
description: An attractive starling. Adult is entirely dark glossy-green with a long, deeply forked tail, a bushy crest, and a gleaming white eye.

name: Sumatran Drongo
rangeDescription: Humid lowlands of sumatra
description: Glossy large-billed drongo with glossy blue-sheened wings and tail. Also note bright red eyes, iridescent speckling around the throat and neck, and flared broad-tipped tail.

name: Strange-tailed Tyrant
rangeDescription: Locally in eastern paraguay, southern brazil, uruguay, and northern argentina
description: Striking flycatcher with a spectacular mating display, in which male flies high into the air and repeatedly pumps tails above and then below body. Endemic to the Iberá marshes of NE Argentina and E Paraguay.
